messages.subject: Shiny app works well in RStudio but barely responds on shinyapps.io
parts:
I wonder if you can help me. 

I've prepared the following code to test Shiny, by mapping the best places to live if you work where I work in the UK. This app responds really well in RStudio. It also uploads fine to my space on shinyapps.io. But, once it has loaded to shinyapps.io, it takes (at best) a minute to do what it did in less than a second in RStudio.

My main questions are therefore:
  • Am I doing something stupid in the code (or is this something else)?
  • How can I amend the code to make it less stupid (or what is that 'something else')?
Many thanks in advance for your help.

-- Robin

______________________________________

ui.R

library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Best home location if you work in Reigate"),
  
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel( 
      h5("Enter your preferences:"),
      br(),
      sliderInput("time.slider", 
                  label = h6("Short commute"),
                  min = 0, max = 10, value = 3),
      br(),
      sliderInput("age.slider", 
                  label = h6("Younger areas"),
                  min = 0, max = 10, value = 3),
      br(),
      sliderInput("expense.slider", 
                  label = h6("Cheap housing"),
                  min = 0, max = 10, value = 3),
      br(),
      sliderInput("crime.slider", 
                  label = h6("Low crime"),
                  min = 0, max = 10, value = 3),
      br(),
      sliderInput("flunkers.slider", 
                  label = h6("Good schools"),
                  min = 0, max = 10, value = 3),
      br(),
      sliderInput("deprived.slider", 
                  label = h6("Undeprived areas"),
                  min = 0, max = 10, value = 3),
      br(),
      sliderInput("n.slider", 
                   label = h6("Show top n areas (from 1 to 20,799)"), 
                   min = 1, max = 20799, value = 30), 
      br(),
      checkboxInput("coastal.checkbox",
                    label = h6("Only coastal areas?"),
                    value = FALSE)
    ),
  
    mainPanel(
      br(),
      h5("Lower scores (in red) are better - South and Mid England only - Please be patient"),
      br(),
      plotOutput("plot"))
)))


server.R

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(magrittr)
library(ggmap)

ScoredAreas1a <- read.csv("data/ScoredAreas1a.csv", header=TRUE)   # size of 4MB
Areas1.df <- read.csv("data/Areas1df.csv", header=TRUE)   # size of 94MB

shinyServer(function(input, output){

  England.map <- get_map(location=c(lon=-0.3, lat=51.65), zoom=8, color="bw")
  
  plotInput <- reactive({
    ScoredAreas1 <- ScoredAreas1a %>%
      mutate(score = (input$time.slider*z.time) + (input$age.slider*z.age) +
               (input$expense.slider*z.expense) + (input$crime.slider*z.crime) +
               (input$flunkers.slider*z.flunkers) + (input$deprived.slider*z.deprived))
    
    Top1 <- ScoredAreas1[with(ScoredAreas1, order(score, id)), ]
    if(input$coastal.checkbox==TRUE){Top1 <- Top1[Top1$coastal==TRUE,]}
    Top1 <- Top1[1:input$n.slider,] %>%
      select(id, score, coastal)
    TopAreas <- left_join(Top1, Areas1.df, by="id")

    p <- ggmap(England.map, extent = "panel") +
      geom_polygon(aes(x=long,y=lat,group=id,fill=score),data=TopAreas) +
      scale_fill_gradient(low='red', high='yellow') +
      xlab("") + ylab("")
  })
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    print(plotInput())
  })
})

Hi,

Your data files are pretty large, and that might be the cause of slow start of your application.
Are you using the same data files locally? If yes, then your data might have been loaded in RStudio when you run your app locally. Can you try clearing your environment and running again. 

And if you think this is an issue only on shinyapps.io, I suggest you post it to this list:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/shinyapps-users


Best,
Fereshteh

parts:
Robin,

These are my observations, running your application locally, and also on shinyapps.io:

- Locally I see a delay of 22-30 s initially to load the map. Is it much faster on your system? If yes, what is your system's configuration?
- On shinyapps.io I also see a delay of about 25 s to load the map. (This is the time after the initial server startup time.) This is what I am seeing today, but I know on Tuesday (Oct 28th) I was seeing much worse behavior from your application. But we figured out there was a problem on shinyapps.io that day. Do you see a difference between Tuesday and today?
- On shinyapps.io, almost any action after the initial load causes your app to crash. I think this is a memory issue. Do you know the size of your application on shinyapps.io?
I monitored memory consumption of your application locally. It takes about 400MB initially when map is loaded. And after that it keeps increasing. The slider at the bottom is the one that uses most memory. I saw memory more than 1G after playing with your app a little bit. So the crash on shinyapps.io might be expected if you are using a small or medium size. Please refer to this guide, section on "Configuring applications" on how to change the size of application. But you should also look into making your application more efficient. 

Best,
Fereshteh

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(magrittr)
library(ggmap)

ScoredAreas1a <- read.csv("data/ScoredAreas1a.csv", header=TRUE)   # size of 4MB
Areas1.df <- read.csv("data/Areas1df.csv", header=TRUE)   # size of 94MB

shinyServer(function(input, output){

  England.map <- get_map(location=c(lon=-0.3, lat=51.65), zoom=8, color="bw")
  
  plotInput <- reactive({
    ScoredAreas1 <- ScoredAreas1a %>%
      mutate(score = (input$time.slider*z.time) + (input$age.slider*z.age) +
               (input$expense.slider*z.expense) + (input$crime.slider*z.crime) +
               (input$flunkers.slider*z.flunkers) + (input$deprived.slider*z.deprived))
    
    Top1 <- ScoredAreas1[with(ScoredAreas1, order(score, id)), ]
    if(input$coastal.checkbox==TRUE){Top1 <- Top1[Top1$coastal==TRUE,]}
    Top1 <- Top1[1:input$n.slider,] %>%
      select(id, score, coastal)
    TopAreas <- left_join(Top1, Areas1.df, by="id")

    p <- ggmap(England.map, extent = "panel") +
      geom_polygon(aes(x=long,y=lat,group=id,fill=score),data=TopAreas) +
      scale_fill_gradient(low='red', high='yellow') +
      xlab("") + ylab("")
  })
  
  output$plot <- renderPlot({
    print(plotInput())
  })
})
